heroEyebrow: A focused CMS for Astro teams
heroTitle: Give editors forms. Keep everything in Git.
heroSummary: Mica turns your content model into a clean editing interface. Editors draft in peace, review what changed, and publish one commit of readable JSON, Markdoc, and media. Your Astro build stays static and independent.
problemEyebrow: Your repository is the source of truth
problemTitle: A CMS should not become part of your website's runtime.
problemSummary: Mica gives non-technical editors a good interface without putting content behind an API. The public website reads local files at build time. It stays fast, portable, and available even when Mica is offline.
workflowTitle: One model. One clear path from edit to website.
workflowSummary: The content model connects the editor and the build. Git connects everything else.

workflowSteps.title: Describe
workflowSteps.text: Define collections, fields, validation, labels, and editor help in one TypeScript module.

workflowSteps.title: Edit
workflowSteps.text: Mica reads the model and gives your team generated forms, media tools, and safe validation.

workflowSteps.title: Ship
workflowSteps.text: Drafts stay with the editor until Publish turns them into one commit. Your existing CI runs Astro and sends static files to any host.

featuresTitle: The content workflow that Git already wanted.
featuresSummary: Mica removes the glue between a content editor and an Astro project. It does not add a second platform to operate.

principles.title: Own the source
principles.text: Content stays in formats that people, Git, and Astro can read without Mica. There is no export step.

principles.title: Use the web you have
principles.text: Keep your repository, CI, static host, and identity provider. Mica fits the path instead of replacing it.

principles.title: Say no on purpose
principles.text: No page builder, GraphQL layer, media server, or custom workflow. The smaller product is the more reliable product.

ctaTitle: Your Astro site is already close.
ctaText: Add two packages, write one content model, and open the editor. Your templates remain ordinary Astro.
